title: Eval playbook for pinned model upgrades and stakeholder notification flow
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: Define and implement an operational playbook that automatically runs a focused eval suite and notifies relevant stakeholders whenever a model version is pinned, upgraded, or when a config change affects inference behavior. This covers both Redwood catalog models and customer-pinned model versions. The playbook should specify which evals run, gating thresholds, notification recipients, and mitigation steps for detected regressions.
background: We already have ad-hoc eval triggers and some pipeline automation for model swaps, but incidents have shown gaps: customer pins sometimes change silently (via managed upgrades), and engineering response is slow for small but high-severity quality regressions. This ticket aims to centralize policy and automate primary/fast-path evals and human-in-the-loop escalations.
goals: Automatically execute a compact eval suite on: (a) model version pin/upgrades in the catalog, (b) customer-requested pin changes, and (c) config diffs that affect tokenization, sampling, or quantization profiles.
Define gating thresholds (metric deltas, confidence intervals) that trigger three tiers: info, investigate, and emergency rollback/fallback.
Deliver a notification and runbook flow so PM/QA/Oncall/Customer Success get clear next steps and links to failing prompts and diffs.
Expose a lightweight dashboard card in Console showing last-eval, delta, and status for pinned models.
Avoid over-triggering: ensure noise suppression via debounce windows and aggregated diffs for bulk updates.
success_criteria: Eval runs automatically within 10 minutes of a pin/upgrade event for catalog changes and within 30 minutes for customer-scoped pin changes.
>90% of detected regressions route to the correct owner (oncall or model-owner) with reproducible failing prompts.
False-positive rate of emergency rollbacks stays below 5% in the first month of rollout.
Console shows per-pin history and last-eval badge for 100% of pinned models in catalog and dedicated customer pins.
Runbook reduces median time-to-detect for regression events by 40% versus today.
user_stories: As an engineering oncall, I want to receive a concise alert with a delta summary and top 10 failing prompts so I can quickly triage whether to failback or investigate.
As a product manager, I want a pre-approved gating threshold that blocks automatic rollout when quality drops more than X% versus baseline so we avoid exposing customers to regressions.
As a customer success rep, I want to be notified when a customer-pinned model upgrade causes a high-severity regression so I can proactively contact the customer.
acceptance_criteria: Event hooks documented and added to model-pin flow (catalog and customer pin APIs) with sample payloads.
Compact eval suite implemented (latency, perplexity/QA accuracy/ROUGE depending on model task) and wired into CI with synthetic and real prompt subsets.
Notification templates created for Slack/email/PagerDuty with links to evaluation run, PRs, model pin diff, and rollback button (where applicable).
Dashboard card implemented in Console prototype and reviewed by UX.
implementation_notes: We will implement a two-stage eval: quick smoke eval (≈100 prompts, subset by task) and full regression eval (≈2k prompts) for cases that cross the investigate threshold. For catalog-managed pins, run smoke eval automatically; for customer pins, run smoke eval and optionally require customer approval for full rollout if thresholds are exceeded. Use existing evals infrastructure, add an event router that deduplicates pin-change events (30m window).
tradeoffs: Aggressive gating reduces customer exposure to regressions but increases friction for rapid performance upgrades. To balance, we choose a tiered approach with a short debounce window and allow model owners to opt into a fast-path bypass for non-breaking changes.
risks: Eval coverage may miss task-specific regressions for niche customers; mitigate by allowing customers to register custom prompt-sets for pinned models.
Notification fatigue if thresholds are too sensitive; mitigate via aggregation and adjustable sensitivity per project.
Performance overhead on eval cluster during bulk catalog updates; mitigate with rate limits and prioritization.
runbook_outline: 1) Alert triggers: smoke eval delta > investigate threshold. 2) Auto-run full regression eval. 3) If full eval crosses emergency threshold, post emergency alert to model-owner, oncall, and CS; include rollback URL. 4) Model-owner triages using top failing prompts and can approve immediate rollback or initiate patch release. 5) Post-incident: collect metrics and add failing prompts to regression watchlist.
notification_routing: Info -> model-owner email + Console banner; Investigate -> Slack channel + ticket in Linear with prefilled reproducible steps; Emergency -> PagerDuty page + CS + oncall escalation.
